# vendor/accelerator: install notes for the kit

This folder holds a scrubbed copy of the Claude Code plugin marketplace: `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` plus each plugin folder. `README.md` next to this file is generated by `tools/gen-readme.py`; never edit it by hand. Kit-specific notes live here.

Install it from this local folder:

```
/plugin marketplace add ${KIT_HOME}/vendor/accelerator
/plugin install ai-baseline@accelerator
/plugin install content-companion@accelerator
```

Install `ai-baseline` first; the other plugins expect it. Its "PII scrub" is an instruction to the model, not a guarantee, and runs after text has been sent. Do not rely on it to protect students' data: keep that data out of prompts.

## Your name, email and homepage

The plugins ship with the placeholder name and email of `kit.config.example.yaml` and no homepage. To put your own in, set `kit.author_name`, `kit.author_email` and, if you want one, `kit.homepage` in `${KIT_HOME}/kit.config.yaml`, then run both generators from this folder:

```
python3 tools/gen-registry.py
python3 tools/gen-readme.py
```

- `gen-registry.py` updates every `plugin.json` (author, homepage) and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (owner, each plugin's author and homepage).
- `gen-readme.py` updates `README.md`, the maintainer lines of the plugin READMEs, the OpenAPI contact in `api-designer`, the author the `assimilator` converter writes, the `dependency-auditor` report footer, and the release check.
- An empty `kit.homepage` removes the homepage fields and turns the builder plugin's release check off, so nothing is fetched. A GitHub repository URL makes the check read that repository's latest release.
- Only the identity values change; running the generators again with the same config changes nothing, and removing the keys (or the file) restores the placeholders. They read `KIT_HOME` from the environment, else the folder two levels above this one.
- If the config is invalid or a doc no longer has its identity line, they stop with the key or file name and write nothing.

## Building your own plugins

`agent-builder` (command `/build-agent`) interviews you, then designs, generates, reviews and writes a new plugin, or audits an existing one. It is a build tool: install it only if you want to make plugins (`/plugin install agent-builder@accelerator`).

## Model prices

The `ai-baseline` hooks cost every agent call with the rates in `pricing.json` in this folder (`accelerator.pricing_table_file` in the kit config), in USD per token. To change a rate, edit that file, then run from this folder:

```
python3 tools/sync-shipped-hooks.py
python3 tools/check-hooks-drift.py
python3 tools/check-model-ids.py
```

- The sync copies the file to `ai-baseline/hooks/scripts/pricing.json`, the copy the installed plugin reads; run `/plugin update ai-baseline@accelerator` afterwards.
- `check-model-ids.py` checks that `pricing.json` prices the same tiers (haiku, sonnet, opus) as `tools/model-ids.json`, which stays the list of model IDs agents may declare.
- If `pricing.json` is missing or broken, the hooks keep the audit log but leave the budget unchanged and print a warning that names the file.
